content: Administer 768 mg of the medication orally twice daily. Continue this treatment for two years or until there is a recurrence of the disease or the development of unacceptable toxicity. If hemoglobin levels drop below 8 g/dL, withhold the medication until recovery to levels of 8 g/dL or higher, then resume at the same dose. If anemia recurs (hemoglobin < 8 g/dL), withhold the medication again until recovery to ≥ 8 g/dL, then resume at the next reduced dose level. For Ornidyl (eflornithine), hypersensitivity to eflornithine or any ingredient in the formulation is a contraindication. The World Health Organization supplies this drug to the CDC for use in treating African trypanosomiasis. Based on animal studies and its mechanism of action, eflornithine may cause fetal harm if administered to pregnant women. Verify pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential before initiating treatment. There are no available data on the use of eflornithine in pregnant women. Inform pregnant women and females of reproductive potential about the potential fetal risks. Additionally, there is no data on the presence of eflornithine in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed children, or its impact on milk production. Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for one week after the last dose. For another medication (A), it is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Administer this medication with or without food. Tablets may be swallowed whole, chewed, or crushed. Store the medication at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions between 15–30°C (59–86°F).
